title: Lessons from the School of Prayer 3 - Worthy Petitions
speaker: Pastor Nick
series: Lessons from the School of Prayer

outline.title: The Context of Paul's Petitions
subpoints: Petitions flow directly from thanksgiving for God's grace
Prayer is a primary means of revival and spiritual reformation
Adopting an eternal perspective shapes the content of prayer

outline.title: Petition 1: Being Counted Worthy of the Calling
subpoints: Understanding the effective call of God
The paradox of becoming what one already is in Christ
Prioritizing spiritual maturity over physical or material needs

outline.title: Petition 2: Fulfillment of Good Pleasures
subpoints: God transforming desires and ambitions through the Spirit
The necessity of divine power to sustain good works
Praying for the fruition of faith-prompted actions

outline.title: Application: Examining Our Prayer Priorities
subpoints: Prayer reveals true values alongside calendars and finances
Parents must prioritize spiritual transformation for their children
Committing to a life of spiritual reformation through prayer

summary:
This sermon, the third installment in the 'Lessons from the School of Prayer' series, examines the worthy petitions found in 2 Thessalonians 1:11-12. The speaker emphasizes that prayer is a vital means of revival and spiritual reformation, urging believers to adopt an eternal perspective that shapes their intercessions. The focus is on understanding how Paul’s petitions flow directly from his thanksgiving for the grace evident in the Thessalonian church.

The first major petition is for believers to be counted worthy of God’s calling. This is explained not as earning salvation, but as growing into Christian maturity and living out the identity already granted in Christ. The sermon challenges listeners to examine their prayer lives, noting that a lack of focus on spiritual growth may indicate misplaced priorities, particularly for parents seeking the holistic well-being of their children.

The second petition is for God to fulfill the good desires and works of faith that the Holy Spirit has instilled in believers. The speaker highlights the necessity of divine power to sustain these efforts, citing Philippians 2:13. The message concludes by encouraging the congregation to align their prayers with these biblical priorities, seeking spiritual transformation and the fulfillment of God’s will above all else.
